panels.title: EPE - Policy Enforcement
panels.description: Whether published policy is actually in effect. `unenforced` is the severe one: those sources have no installed version at all, so none of their rules run and the Pods they select are unprotected. `stale` means an older version is still enforcing because the newest one was rejected. `inputs unavailable` means the rules do run, but a referenced ConfigMap input is missing, so inputs-dependent actions fail per their failure strategy. The scope label says who acts: namespaced/global are operator profiles matched by label selector, pod is one tenant's Sandbox annotation matched by Pod identity. These are counts by design — the EPE logs name the object and the error. Aggregated with max, not sum: every EPE replica watches the same policy and publishes the same value, so summing would multiply it by the replica count. The request-path panels sum because requests are split across replicas.

panels.title: EPE - Rejected Policy Versions
panels.description: Rate of published policy versions EPE refused to compile. Use it to confirm a rollout landed: a rejection that was published and then fixed shows here even though the enforcement panel is back to zero. Aggregated with max, not sum: every EPE replica watches the same policy and publishes the same value, so summing would multiply it by the replica count. The request-path panels sum because requests are split across replicas.
